title: Fourteen Goals. Zero Conceded. India's Women Have Been Perfect in the SAFF Championship. The Semi-Final Is Next.
excerpt: The Blue Tigresses face Bhutan on Wednesday in Goa after demolishing the Maldives 11-0 and beating defending champions Bangladesh 3-0 in the group stage.
body:
India's women's football team has been ruthless. Two group-stage matches in the 2026 SAFF Women's Championship, hosted in Goa, have produced fourteen goals scored and zero conceded. The Blue Tigresses topped Group B and will face Bhutan in the semi-final at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Margao on Wednesday, June 3.

The Numbers Tell the Story

The opener against the Maldives was not a match — it was a statement. India won 11-0, with striker Aveka Singh scoring four goals and claiming the Player of the Match award. The Næstved HG midfielder, who plays her club football in Denmark, was unstoppable in front of goal, combining inch-perfect through balls with a knack for arriving late in the box.

Against defending champions Bangladesh, India showed a different dimension. The 3-0 victory was controlled, tactical, and clinical. Pyari Xaxa anchored the midfield while forwards Win Theingi Tun Kom and others provided the cutting edge. Two clean sheets in two matches — the defensive discipline has been as impressive as the attacking firepower.

Aveka Singh: The X-Factor

Singh is the tournament's leading scorer and the player opponents least want to face. Her European experience with Næstved HG in Denmark has sharpened her game — the physicality, the pace, the decision-making under pressure. For the growing number of Indian women footballers plying their trade in European lower divisions, Singh's performances in a national team shirt are proof that the pathway works.

Her supporting cast has been equally impressive. Xaxa's ball-winning ability in midfield gives India a platform; Soumya Guguloth provides width; and goalkeeper Shreya Hooda has barely been tested — a testament to how thoroughly India have controlled both matches.

Bhutan Will Not Be Easy

Bhutan are no pushovers in the semi-final. They finished second in Group A after a narrow 0-1 loss to Nepal was followed by a commanding 4-0 demolition of Sri Lanka. Tshering scored a hat-trick in that match, and Lhazom added another. Bhutan have reached the semi-finals in each of the last two editions and have found a consistency that belies their FIFA ranking.

The last time these two teams met was in 2010 — in the inaugural SAFF Women's Championship in Bangladesh. India won 18-0, with Bala Devi scoring five and Sasmita Mallik seven. The gulf has narrowed since then, though India remain overwhelming favourites.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

Women's football in India has long been an afterthought — underfunded, under-covered, and invisible to most of the country's sports audience. But this SAFF Championship team, coached by Crispin Chettri, represents something different: a generation of players with professional experience abroad, a tactical sophistication that goes beyond raw athleticism, and a hunger that comes from knowing how little attention they receive.

For NRIs who follow Indian sport primarily through cricket and occasionally through badminton or chess, the Blue Tigresses are a blind spot worth correcting. Fourteen goals in two matches is not a statistic that happens by accident.

What Is Next

The semi-final against Bhutan is on Wednesday, June 3, at 8:00 PM IST (10:30 AM ET / 7:30 AM PT) at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Margao, Goa. The match will be live-streamed on FanCode.

If India win — and they are expected to — the final is on Saturday, June 7. Nepal, the other Group A topper, are the likely opponents. A title defence is within reach, but first, the Blue Tigresses must maintain the standard they have set: total dominance, zero goals conceded, and the kind of football that demands attention.

The 2026 SAFF Women's Championship runs from May 25 to June 7 at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Margao, Goa.
